items.item: Month and week views, a Today button and previous/next navigation, with the visible range written as text (such as "November 2026")
items.evidence: #segMonth/#segWeek toggle buttons (data-action="view-month"/"view-week"), data-action="prev"/"next"/"today" buttons, and #periodLabel which renders fmtMonthYear(state.refDate) → visible text "November 2026" (confirmed in screenshot).

items.item: Today is marked, and weekends and public holidays are distinguishable by text or a legend, not by colour alone
items.evidence: Today is marked only by a solid blue circle around the day number (dayNumCls with bg-blue-700, no text badge). Public holidays do get a text label (holiday.label, e.g. "Thanksgiving Day" rendered in the cell and legend entry 'Public holiday'), but weekend columns (Sun/Sat) receive no distinguishing treatment at all — cellCls only varies by in-month vs out-of-month (bg-white/bg-slate-50), with no weekend styling, text, or legend entry.

items.item: Each leave shows the person and leave type in text, and pending requests differ from approved ones by text or a pattern, not by colour alone
items.evidence: entryChipHtml() (month grid, the primary view) renders only the employee name as visible text; leave type is conveyed solely by an aria-hidden colored dot (span.size-1.5...type.dot) with the type label only present in the title/aria-label, not visibly rendered. Status differentiation does use non-color patterns (dashed border + clock icon for pending, line-through text for rejected), which is good, but the missing visible leave-type text fails this item.

items.item: A leave of several days spans its days continuously, and a crowded day shows "+N more" that opens the full list instead of hiding entries
items.evidence: Multi-day leaves are rendered independently per day: requestsOnDate(iso) is recomputed for every <td> and entryChipHtml() draws a fully-rounded standalone chip in each day's cell (visible in screenshot as separate pills for 'Elena Rossi' repeated day after day) rather than one continuous bar spanning the date range. The "+N more" button (more>0 branch) does correctly call data-action="open-day" → openDayModal(iso), which lists the full day's entries instead of hiding them, so only that half of the requirement is met.

items.item: Days where many people are off are flagged with a count (such as "3 of 8 off")
items.evidence: No such count exists anywhere in renderMonth()/renderWeek() or openDayModal(); cells only show the leave chips themselves and a generic "+N more" overflow link, never an "X of Y off" style flag.

items.item: Opening a leave shows its absolute dates, its length in working days and its status, with approve and reject actions for pending requests
items.evidence: openDayModal() shows absolute dates (fmtRange(r.start, r.end)) and a status badge, plus Approve/Reject buttons for pending items (data-action="approve"/"open-reject"). However, it never shows the leave's length at all (no days count in the modal), and the only place a day count is shown (pending table's daysCount()) is total calendar days, not working days (no weekend/holiday exclusion).

items.item: The calendar is keyboard operable (arrow keys in the grid, or every entry reachable in tab order), and entries have accessible names that include the date
items.evidence: No arrow-key grid navigation is implemented (only an Escape handler on document keydown), but every leave entry is a native <button data-action="open-day"> so is reachable via Tab. However entry accessible names fail to reliably include the date: entryChipHtml()'s aria-label only appends a date range for multi-day leaves (`req.start !== req.end ? ", " + fmtRange(...) : ""`), omitting it for single-day leaves, and the week-view cell label (`emp.name + " — " + type.label + " (" + status.label + ")"`) never includes a date at all.

items.item: Filters by team, person or leave type, and a list view as an alternative to the grid
items.evidence: #deptSelect (team/department), #searchInput (person by name), and #typeSelect (leave type) filters are all present and wired up. But there is no list view: the only views are the Month/Week grid toggle (#segMonth/#segWeek); the 'Pending approval' table is a separate fixed sub-section for pending requests only, not a selectable list alternative to the full calendar grid.

items.item: Weeks start on the locale's first day, dates follow the locale, and empty, loading and error states are present
items.evidence: startOfWeekISO() and monthGridDates() hardcode a Sunday week start (`d.setUTCDate(d.getUTCDate() - d.getUTCDay())`) regardless of locale, while all date formatting is hardcoded to "en-GB" (new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-GB", ...)) rather than following the user's actual locale — and en-GB convention itself starts weeks on Monday, so the fixed Sunday grid is inconsistent with the locale it claims to format for. Empty/loading/error states are implemented correctly (skeletonHtml(), emptyStateHtml(), errorStateHtml() driven by ?state= query param), satisfying only that clause.

notes: No template tells observed: no gradients/glass/emoji/uppercase tracked labels (confirmed by audit.json's no-gradient/no-backdrop-blur/uppercase-text/emoji-icon rules passing), avatars use real employee initials (legitimate person avatars, not decorative), status colors form a reasonable semantic triad rather than a rainbow, and there are no promo cards, decorative charts, or nested card-in-card sections. Automated audit (run-1.audit.json) scored 70/100, flagging numeric-align, tabular-nums, and text-contrast violations (e.g. day-number buttons and the Ctrl K kbd hint at 2.45:1 contrast) which are independent of this checklist but worth noting.
